questions.q:
A rectangular photograph is 96 mm wide and 72 mm high.
(a) Write the ratio of its width to its height in simplest form, naming the HCF you divide by.
(b) The same photograph is turned on its side so that it is 72 mm wide and 96 mm high. Is the width-to-height ratio still the same? Explain what changed.
questions.a: (a) The HCF of 96 and 72 is 24, so 96 : 72 = 4 : 3. (b) No. The width-to-height ratio is now 72 : 96 = 3 : 4. The lengths are the same, but the first term of the ratio now stands for 72 mm, so the order of the terms, and the ratio, has changed.
s: Part (a): HCF 24 and the ratio 4 : 3
Part (b): the new ratio 3 : 4, with the reason that the order of the terms changed

questions.q: True or False: If the ratio of boys to girls in a class is 3 : 4, then the class must have exactly 7 students. Give a reason.
questions.a: False. The ratio 3 : 4 only says that for every 3 boys there are 4 girls. The class could have 3 boys and 4 girls, or 9 boys and 12 girls (21 students), or 15 boys and 20 girls (35 students); the total can be any multiple of 7.
s: States False

questions.q: Arjun says: 'The ratio 26 : 39 is already in its simplest form. One term is even and the other is odd, so they cannot have a common factor other than 1.' Is Arjun right? Check his reason and give the correct simplest form.
questions.a: No. An even number and an odd number cannot share the factor 2, but they can share an odd factor. 26 = 2 x 13 and 39 = 3 x 13, so the HCF is 13. Dividing both terms by 13 gives 2 : 3, which is the simplest form.
s: Shows that 26 and 39 share the factor 13
Explains that 'even and odd' only rules out the common factor 2
Gives the verdict No and the simplest form 2 : 3

A notice board is 1.5 m wide and 90 cm high.
(a) Write the ratio of its width to its height in simplest form, after writing both in the same unit.
(b) A ribbon is fixed all round its edge. Write the ratio of the board's height to the length of the ribbon in simplest form.
questions.a: (a) 1.5 m = 150 cm, so the ratio is 150 : 90. The HCF is 30, giving 5 : 3. (b) The ribbon is the perimeter, 2 x (150 + 90) = 480 cm. The ratio 90 : 480 has HCF 30, giving 3 : 16.
s: Part (a): 150 : 90 reduced to 5 : 3
Part (b): ribbon 480 cm and the ratio 3 : 16

questions.q:
A ratio in simplest form is 3 : 5, and the HCF of its two original terms was 12.
(a) Find the original ratio.
(b) Write a real situation, with units, that the original ratio could describe, and say what 'for every' means in it.
(c) Explain why someone told only '3 : 5' could not find the original numbers.
questions.a: (a) Multiplying back by the HCF gives 36 : 60. (b) For example, a cricket coaching camp has 36 boys and 60 girls: for every 3 boys there are 5 girls. (c) Every ratio 3k : 5k (6 : 10, 9 : 15, 36 : 60, ...) reduces to 3 : 5, so the simplest form does not tell which multiple was used; the HCF is needed.
s: Part (b): a sensible situation with units and the 'for every' reading
Part (c): many ratios reduce to 3 : 5, so the HCF is needed

questions.q:
A tea stall near a bus depot counts its sales. On Monday it sold 168 cups of tea and 72 cups of coffee. On Tuesday it sold 150 cups of tea and 90 cups of coffee. The owner puts up a 'Tea Special' board on any day when at least 2 cups of tea are sold for every 1 cup of coffee.
(a) Write the tea-to-coffee ratio for Monday in simplest form.
(b) Write the tea-to-coffee ratio for Tuesday in simplest form.
(c) On which day were more cups of tea sold for every cup of coffee? Compare your two ratios.
(d) On which day or days should the 'Tea Special' board have been up? Justify using your ratios.
questions.a: (a) HCF of 168 and 72 is 24, so 7 : 3. (b) HCF of 150 and 90 is 30, so 5 : 3. (c) Both ratios have second term 3, so compare first terms: 7 > 5, so Monday had more tea for every cup of coffee. (d) 2 : 1 is the same as 6 : 3. Monday's 7 : 3 is more than 6 : 3, so the board should be up; Tuesday's 5 : 3 is less than 6 : 3, so not. Only Monday.
s: Part (a): 7 : 3
Part (b): 5 : 3
Part (c): Monday, comparing 7 : 3 with 5 : 3
Part (d): only Monday, writing 2 : 1 as 6 : 3

questions.q: Show that the ratio of boys to girls in a class of 36 students cannot be 3 : 5.
questions.a: A ratio of 3 : 5 means that for every 3 boys there are 5 girls, so the students come in groups of 3 + 5 = 8. The class size would have to be a multiple of 8. 36 is not a multiple of 8 (8 x 4 = 32 and 8 x 5 = 40), so the ratio cannot be 3 : 5.
s: Explains that each 'for every' group has 3 + 5 = 8 students
States that the total must be a multiple of 8
Shows that 36 is not a multiple of 8

Two numbers are in the ratio 5 : 8 in simplest form, and the larger number is 27 more than the smaller.
(a) How many 'units' of the ratio does the difference of 27 stand for?
(b) Find the two numbers and check your answer.
questions.a: (a) The terms are 5 parts and 8 parts, so the difference is 8 - 5 = 3 parts, and 3 parts = 27, giving 1 part = 9. (b) The numbers are 5 x 9 = 45 and 8 x 9 = 72. Check: 72 - 45 = 27, and the HCF of 45 and 72 is 9, so 45 : 72 = 5 : 8.
s: Part (a): the difference is 3 parts, so 1 part = 9
Part (b): 45 and 72 with a check

questions.a: (a) For example 6, 12 and 20 are common factors: 180 : 240 becomes 30 : 40, 15 : 20 and 9 : 12. Each of these can still be reduced (30 : 40 by 10, 15 : 20 by 5, 9 : 12 by 3). (b) 180 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 3 x 5 and 240 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 5, so the HCF is 2 x 2 x 3 x 5 = 60, and 180 : 240 = 3 : 4. (c) The HCF takes out every common factor at once. What is left, 3 and 4, has HCF 1, so no other common factor remains. A smaller common factor leaves some common factor behind, which is why the statement is justified.

questions.a: (a) 132 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 11 and 198 = 2 x 3 x 3 x 11, so the HCF is 2 x 3 x 11 = 66, and 132 : 198 = 2 : 3. (b) The HCF of 2 and 3 is 1; they have no common factor other than 1, so the ratio cannot be reduced further.
s: Part (a): HCF 66 and 2 : 3
Part (b): the terms 2 and 3 have HCF 1

questions.q:
A school is choosing devices for video lessons. The screens are listed in pixels as width x height: a laptop 1920 x 1080, a tablet 1024 x 768 and a phone 2400 x 1080. A video fills a screen with no black bands only when the screen's width-to-height ratio is the same as the video's. The lesson videos are made in the ratio 16 : 9.
(a) Write the laptop's width-to-height ratio in simplest form.
(b) Write the tablet's and the phone's ratios in simplest form.
(c) A classroom projector shows a picture in the same ratio as the laptop. The picture is 2.7 m high. How wide is it?
(d) Which of the three devices should the school buy so that the videos show with no black bands? Justify.
questions.a: (a) HCF of 1920 and 1080 is 120, so 16 : 9. (b) Tablet: HCF 256, so 4 : 3. Phone: HCF 120, so 20 : 9. (c) For every 9 units of height there are 16 of width: 2.7 is 9 x 0.3, so the width is 16 x 0.3 = 4.8 m. (d) The laptop, because only its ratio 16 : 9 matches the videos; 4 : 3 and 20 : 9 are different ratios, so those screens would show bands.
s: Part (a): 16 : 9
Part (b): 4 : 3 and 20 : 9
Part (c): 4.8 m
Part (d): the laptop, as only its ratio matches 16 : 9

(a) Write the ratio of rent to food in simplest form.
(b) Write the ratio of food to travel in simplest form.
(c) Next month travel goes up by Rs 1,050 and food and rent stay the same. Write the new ratio of food to travel in simplest form.
(d) The father says, 'Rent was 4 times travel before, and it is still 4 times travel now.' Check his claim using a ratio.
(e) For the first month, a relative says 'for every Rs 4 of rent there is Rs 1 of travel'. Is this a correct reading? Explain.
questions.a: (a) HCF of 12,600 and 9,450 is 3,150, so 4 : 3. (b) 9,450 : 3,150 = 3 : 1. (c) Travel becomes 4,200. HCF of 9,450 and 4,200 is 1,050, so 9 : 4. (d) Before: 12,600 : 3,150 = 4 : 1. Now: 12,600 : 4,200 = 3 : 1. Rent is now only 3 times travel, so he is wrong. (e) Yes. In the first month rent : travel = 4 : 1, which reads 'for every Rs 4 of rent, Rs 1 of travel'.
s: Part (a): 4 : 3
Part (b): 3 : 1
Part (c): 9 : 4
Part (d): new ratio 3 : 1, so the claim is wrong
Part (e): yes, 4 : 1 read as 'for every'

questions.q: True or False: If a : b :: c : d, and both a : b and c : d are already in their simplest forms, then a = c and b = d. Give a reason.
questions.a: True. Two ratios are proportional exactly when their simplest forms are the same. If a : b and c : d are already in simplest form, each is its own simplest form, so they must be the same ratio: a = c and b = d. For example, the only ratio in simplest form that is proportional to 2 : 5 is 2 : 5 itself.

(b) Which copy looks like the poster without distortion? Explain using your factors.
questions.a: (a) Copy P: width 75/90 = 5/6, height 54/60 = 9/10. Copy Q: width 60/90 = 2/3, height 40/60 = 2/3. (b) Copy Q, because its width and height changed by the same factor (2/3), so the change is proportional. Copy P's width and height changed by different factors (5/6 and 9/10), so it looks distorted: its height shrank less than its width.
s: Part (a): factors 5/6 and 9/10 for P, and 2/3 and 2/3 for Q
Part (b): Copy Q, since only its two factors are equal

questions.a: 12 : 18 in simplest form is 2 : 3 (HCF 6), and 28 : 12 in simplest form is 7 : 3 (HCF 4). The simplest forms differ, so the statement is false. For 2 : 3 :: 28 : d, 28 is 14 times 2, so d = 3 x 14 = 42. The true statement is 12 : 18 :: 28 : 42.

Reduces 28 : 12 to 7 : 3 and concludes it is not a proportion

At a school fete, 8 glasses of lemonade are made with 12 spoons of sugar.
(a) How many spoons of sugar are needed for 20 glasses with the same sweetness?
(b) Ishan has only 21 spoons of sugar left. How many glasses of the same sweetness can he make? Show that his batch and the batch in (a) are proportional to each other.
questions.a: (a) 20 / 8 = 5/2, so the sugar is 12 x 5/2 = 30 spoons. (b) 21 / 12 = 7/4, so he can make 8 x 7/4 = 14 glasses. His batch is 14 : 21 = 2 : 3 (HCF 7) and the batch in (a) is 20 : 30 = 2 : 3 (HCF 10). The simplest forms are the same, so 14 : 21 :: 20 : 30.
s: Part (a): 30 spoons
Part (b): 14 glasses, with both batches reduced to 2 : 3

questions.q:
A coffee shop's regular coffee uses 15 mL of decoction for every 35 mL of milk. A coffee with more decoction for the same milk is 'stronger'; with less, it is 'lighter'.
(a) Write the regular ratio of decoction to milk in simplest form.
(b) Classify each mix as regular, stronger or lighter: 90 : 210, 60 : 90, 40 : 120 (decoction : milk, in mL). Show your comparison.
(c) The owner has 84 mL of decoction left. How much milk does he need to make regular coffee with all of it?
(d) A trainee adds 10 mL to both the decoction and the milk of one regular cup, making 25 : 45, and says the taste will not change. Is the trainee right? Explain.
questions.a: (a) 15 : 35 = 3 : 7. (b) 90 : 210 = 3 : 7, regular. 60 : 90 = 2 : 3 = 14 : 21, while regular is 3 : 7 = 9 : 21; more decoction for the same milk, so stronger. 40 : 120 = 1 : 3 = 7 : 21, less than 9 : 21, so lighter. (c) 84 is 28 times 3, so the milk is 7 x 28 = 196 mL. (d) No. 25 : 45 = 5 : 9 = 35 : 63, while regular is 3 : 7 = 27 : 63. For the same milk the trainee's cup has more decoction, so it is stronger: adding the same amount to both terms changed the ratio.
s: Part (a): 3 : 7
Part (b): 90 : 210 regular and 60 : 90 stronger, with a comparison
Part (b): 40 : 120 lighter, with a comparison
Part (c): 196 mL of milk
Part (d): no; 5 : 9 is not 3 : 7, so the cup is stronger

questions.q:
The school magazine has a photo 60 mm wide and 45 mm high. The editor needs three versions with no distortion: a thumbnail 24 mm wide, a cover picture 160 mm wide, and a banner for a slot that is exactly 96 mm wide and 75 mm high. Designer P sends a banner 100 mm wide and 75 mm high and says, 'It is in proportion and uses the full height.' Designer Q stretches the photo to 96 mm by 75 mm so that it fills the slot exactly.
(a) Write the photo's width-to-height ratio in simplest form.
(b) Find the height of the thumbnail.
(c) Find the height of the cover picture.
(d) Should the editor use P's banner, Q's banner, or a different size? Justify using ratios and the slot's measurements.
questions.a: (a) HCF of 60 and 45 is 15, so 4 : 3. (b) 24 is 6 times 4, so the height is 3 x 6 = 18 mm. (c) 160 is 40 times 4, so the height is 3 x 40 = 120 mm. (d) Neither. P's banner is 100 : 75 = 4 : 3, so it is not distorted, but it is 4 mm wider than the 96 mm slot and does not fit. Q's banner is 96 : 75 = 32 : 25 (HCF 3), which is not 4 : 3, so the photo is stretched in height. A banner 96 mm wide in proportion needs a height of 3 x 24 = 72 mm (96 is 24 times 4): 96 : 72 = 4 : 3 and it fits, leaving only 3 mm of the height unused. The editor should use 96 mm by 72 mm.
s: Part (a): 4 : 3
Part (b): 18 mm
Part (c): 120 mm
Part (d): 96 mm by 72 mm, since P's 4 : 3 banner is too wide and Q's 32 : 25 is distorted

questions.q:
A district office lists four schools.
School A: 6 teachers, 168 students
School B: 9 teachers, 279 students
School C: 12 teachers, 336 students
School D: 5 teachers, 150 students
The district gives one extra teacher to any school with more than 30 students for every 1 teacher.
(a) Write the teacher-to-student ratios of Schools A and B in simplest form.
(b) Which other school's ratio is proportional to School A's? Show it.
(c) A new School E has a teacher-to-student ratio proportional to School D's and has 8 teachers. How many students does it have?
(d) Which school or schools get an extra teacher? After the extra teacher joins, does that school still have more than 30 students for every teacher? Justify.
questions.a: (a) A: 6 : 168 = 1 : 28. B: 9 : 279 = 1 : 31. (b) School C: 12 : 336 = 1 : 28, the same as A, so 6 : 168 :: 12 : 336. (c) D is 5 : 150 = 1 : 30, so 8 teachers have 8 x 30 = 240 students. (d) Only School B has more than 30 students for each teacher (1 : 31); A and C have 1 : 28 and D has exactly 1 : 30. With one more teacher B has 10 : 279. Ten teachers at 30 each would cover 300 students, and 279 is fewer, so B is no longer above 30 students per teacher.
s: Part (a): 1 : 28 and 1 : 31
Part (b): School C, 1 : 28
Part (c): 240 students
Part (d): only School B; with 10 teachers 279 is under 300, so it is no longer above 30

(a) Write a real situation, with units, in which checking 6 : 4 :: 15 : 10 answers a sensible question. Say what each of the four numbers stands for.
(b) Show whether the statement of proportion is true.
(c) Change exactly one of the four numbers so that the answer to your question in (a) is reversed, and show that it is.
questions.a: (a) For example: a juice stall uses 6 cups of water for every 4 cups of mango pulp; a second stall uses 15 cups of water with 10 cups of pulp. Does the second stall's juice taste the same? 6 and 15 are cups of water; 4 and 10 are cups of pulp. (b) 6 : 4 = 3 : 2 (HCF 2) and 15 : 10 = 3 : 2 (HCF 5). The simplest forms are the same, so the statement is true and the juice tastes the same. (c) For example, change 10 to 12: 15 : 12 = 5 : 4 (HCF 3), which is not 3 : 2, so the second stall's juice would now taste different (it has more pulp for the same water).
s: Part (a): a sensible situation with matching units and the meaning of each number
Part (b): both ratios reduce to 3 : 2, so it is true
Part (c): a one-number change that breaks the proportion, checked in simplest form

questions.q:
A mother is 32 years old and her son is 8. The difference between their ages never changes.
(a) Write the ratio of the mother's age to the son's age now, in simplest form.
(b) After how many years will the ratio be 3 : 1? Check your answer.
(c) After how many years will the ratio be 2 : 1?
(d) Explain why the ratio of their ages can never be 1 : 1.
(e) Can the ratio ever be 4 : 1 again in the future? Use the difference in their ages to justify.
questions.a: (a) 32 : 8 = 4 : 1. (b) The difference is always 32 - 8 = 24 years. In 3 : 1 the mother has 2 parts more than the son, so 2 parts = 24 and 1 part = 12: the son will be 12 and the mother 36, which is after 4 years. Check: 36 : 12 = 3 : 1. (c) In 2 : 1 the difference is 1 part, so 1 part = 24: the son will be 24 and the mother 48, after 16 years. (d) The mother is always 24 years older, so the two terms are never equal. (e) No. In 4 : 1 the difference is 3 parts, so 3 parts = 24 and 1 part = 8; the son must be 8, which is true only now. In the future the ratio will not be 4 : 1 again.
s: Part (a): 4 : 1
Part (b): 2 parts = 24, so after 4 years, ages 36 and 12
Part (c): 1 part = 24, so after 16 years, ages 48 and 24
Part (d): the difference of 24 years never disappears
Part (e): no; 3 parts = 24 forces the son to be 8, which is only now

A school cook makes 18 kg of rice for 150 students. Meena wants the amount for 125 students. She writes 150 : 18 :: 125 : d and then d = (150 x 125) / 18, about 1,042 kg. She says she has used Aryabhata's rule. Is she right? Name the pramana, phala and ichchha, and find the correct amount.
questions.a: No. In 150 : 18 :: 125 : d the pramana is 150 students, the phala is 18 kg and the ichchha is 125 students. Aryabhata's rule multiplies the phala by the ichchha and divides by the pramana: d = (18 x 125) / 150 = 15 kg. Meena multiplied the pramana by the ichchha instead; her 1,042 kg is also absurd, since fewer students cannot need more rice.
s: Names pramana 150 students, phala 18 kg, ichchha 125 students
Applies phala x ichchha / pramana to get 15 kg
Gives the verdict No and names her error

questions.q: Four groups in an art class mix white and blue paint and write down their amounts as white : blue (in mL). Which pair of groups used the paints in proportion? Check by cross multiplying.

(a) Use cross multiplication to find d in 7 : 12 :: 17.5 : d.
(b) Check your answer another way, by finding the factor that takes 7 to 17.5.
s: Part (a): 7d = 210, so d = 30
Part (b): the factor 2.5 gives 12 x 2.5 = 30

questions.q: True or False: If a : b :: c : d, then a : c :: b : d is also a true proportion. Give a reason.
questions.a: True. a : b :: c : d gives a x d = b x c. For a : c :: b : d the cross products are a x d and c x b, which are the same two products, so they are equal and the second proportion is true too (for example 2 : 3 :: 4 : 6 gives 2 : 4 :: 3 : 6).
s: States True
Shows that both proportions need the same equality a x d = b x c

questions.q:
A student derives the cross multiplication rule for a : b :: c : d, starting from c = fa and d = fb.
Statement 1: From c = fa and d = fb we get f = a/c and f = b/d.
Statement 2: Multiplying both sides of c/a = d/b by ab gives bc = ad.
Statement 3: If 5 : 8 :: 20 : d, then d = (8 x 20) / 5 = 32.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 2 and 3 only

questions.q: A road crew knows that a 12 m stretch of footpath needs about 1,500 paver blocks. The footpaths in a park all have the same width and add up to 84 m. About how many paver blocks does the park need?

At a village fair, a farmer gives 1 3/4 kg of jaggery for every 2/3 of a basket of mangoes he receives. How much jaggery must he give for 4 baskets of mangoes?
Write the proportion, solve it by cross multiplication, and check your answer by first finding the jaggery given for 1 basket.
questions.a: Baskets : jaggery gives 2/3 : 1 3/4 :: 4 : d. Cross multiplying, (2/3) x d = 1 3/4 x 4 = 7/4 x 4 = 7, so d = 7 x 3/2 = 21/2 = 10 1/2 kg. Check: for 1 basket the jaggery is 7/4 / (2/3) = 7/4 x 3/2 = 21/8 kg, and 4 x 21/8 = 21/2 = 10 1/2 kg, which matches.
s: Writes 2/3 : 1 3/4 :: 4 : d with the baskets in matching places
Cross multiplies to get d = 10 1/2 kg
Checks with 21/8 kg for 1 basket, times 4

questions.q:
In a Rule of Three problem about a hostel's dal, the phala is 18 kg, the ichchha is 45 students and the ichchhaphala is 54 kg. The pramana is missing.
(a) Write the cross multiplication equation that links the four terms.
(b) Find the pramana and say what it stands for.
questions.a: (a) pramana : phala :: ichchha : ichchhaphala, so pramana x 54 = 18 x 45. (b) pramana = 810 / 54 = 15, so 18 kg of dal is the amount for 15 students.
s: Part (a): pramana x 54 = 18 x 45
Part (b): pramana 15 students

questions.q: A jeweller prices silver chains by weight: a 14 g chain costs Rs 1,330. A matching bracelet weighs 9.8 g. At the same rate, what does the bracelet cost?
questions.a: Rs 931

questions.q:
Let a : b :: c : d, with c = fa and d = fb for the same factor f.
(a) Show that a x d and b x c are both equal to f x a x b.
(b) Use the rule to decide, without simplifying either ratio, whether 9 : 14 :: 27 : 42.
questions.a: (a) a x d = a x (f x b) = f x a x b, and b x c = b x (f x a) = f x a x b, so ad = bc. (b) 9 x 42 = 378 and 14 x 27 = 378. The cross products are equal, so 9 : 14 :: 27 : 42 is true.
s: Part (a): substitutes c = fa and d = fb to get fab both times
Part (b): 378 = 378, so the proportion is true

questions.q: A shop sells 7 identical erasers for Rs 5. Show that, at the same rate, 3 erasers cannot cost a whole number of rupees. Then list every number of erasers from 1 to 20 that does cost a whole number of rupees.
questions.a: 7 : 5 :: 3 : d gives 7d = 5 x 3 = 15, so d = 15/7 = 2 1/7 rupees, not a whole number. In general n erasers cost 5n/7 rupees, which is whole only when 5n is a multiple of 7. Since 5 and 7 have no common factor, n must be a multiple of 7. From 1 to 20 that is 7 erasers (Rs 5) and 14 erasers (Rs 10).
s: Finds the cost of 3 erasers as 15/7 rupees
Explains that n must be a multiple of 7 for 5n/7 to be whole
Lists 7 and 14

questions.q:
A mason finds that an 8 ft length of wall needs 1,120 bricks. He is building a two-room store. Its outer walls are 16 ft, 12 ft, 16 ft and 12 ft long, and one inside wall of 12 ft separates the rooms. All walls have the same height and thickness. Bricks are sold in loads of 2,000 for Rs 13,000 a load, or loose at Rs 7.50 per brick.
(a) Find the total length of wall.
(b) Use the Rule of Three to find the number of bricks needed.
(c) Compare buying 5 full loads with buying 4 loads and the rest loose. Which is cheaper for the store, and by how much?
(d) The owner then adds a 6 ft garden wall of the same height and thickness. How many bricks does it need, and how many bricks are needed in all?
(e) The mason plans to buy for both jobs together using the cheaper plan from (c): 4 loads and the rest loose. The owner says that 5 loads and the rest loose is now cheaper. Who is right? Justify with the costs.
questions.a: (a) 16 + 12 + 16 + 12 + 12 = 68 ft. (b) 8 : 1,120 :: 68 : d, so d = 1,120 x 68 / 8 = 9,520 bricks. (c) 5 loads cost 5 x 13,000 = Rs 65,000. 4 loads give 8,000 bricks for Rs 52,000, and the other 1,520 loose cost 1,520 x 7.50 = Rs 11,400, a total of Rs 63,400. Buying 4 loads and the rest loose is cheaper by Rs 1,600. (d) 8 : 1,120 :: 6 : d gives d = 1,120 x 6 / 8 = 840 bricks, so 9,520 + 840 = 10,360 bricks in all. (e) The owner is right. 4 loads and 2,360 loose cost 52,000 + 2,360 x 7.50 = 52,000 + 17,700 = Rs 69,700. 5 loads and 360 loose cost 65,000 + 360 x 7.50 = 65,000 + 2,700 = Rs 67,700, which is Rs 2,000 less. The extra 840 bricks make a fifth load worth buying.
s: Part (a): 68 ft
Part (b): 9,520 bricks
Part (c): Rs 63,400 against Rs 65,000, so 4 loads and loose, cheaper by Rs 1,600
Part (d): 840 bricks, 10,360 in all
Part (e): the owner is right: Rs 67,700 against Rs 69,700

questions.q:
A kheer recipe for 4 people uses 300 g of rice, 450 mL of milk and 120 g of sugar. The family will serve kheer to 14 people in all. They have 360 g of sugar at home. The shop sells sugar in 50 g sachets at Rs 9 each and in 250 g packets at Rs 24 each. The host will serve all 14 unless the extra sugar costs more than Rs 20; otherwise she will serve only as many as the sugar at home allows.
(a) How much rice is needed for 14 people?
(b) How much milk is needed for 14 people?
(c) How many people can the sugar already at home serve?
(d) Should the family buy sugar (and if so, which) or serve fewer people? Justify with numbers.
questions.a: (a) 4 : 300 :: 14 : d, so d = 300 x 14 / 4 = 1,050 g. (b) 450 x 14 / 4 = 1,575 mL. (c) 120 : 4 :: 360 : n, so n = 4 x 360 / 120 = 12 people. (d) 14 people need 120 x 14 / 4 = 420 g, which is 60 g more than they have. One 250 g packet covers it but costs Rs 24, more than Rs 20. One 50 g sachet is not enough, but two sachets give 100 g for 2 x 9 = Rs 18, which is within Rs 20. So they should buy two 50 g sachets and serve all 14.
s: Part (a): 1,050 g of rice
Part (b): 1,575 mL of milk
Part (c): 12 people
Part (d): needs 60 g more; two sachets for Rs 18 (not the Rs 24 packet), so serve all 14

questions.q:
A solar panel on a school roof produced 18 units of electricity in 4 hours of sunshine. Assume the units produced are proportional to the hours of sunshine. In a typical week the panel gets 6 hours of sunshine on each of 6 days. The science lab uses 60 units a week and the computer lab uses 110 units a week.
(a) How many units does the panel produce in 7 hours of sunshine?
(b) How many hours of sunshine does it need to produce 45 units?
(c) How many units does the panel produce in a typical week?
(d) Can the week's output run the science lab alone, and can it run both labs together? Justify using your answer to (c).
questions.a: (a) 4 : 18 :: 7 : d, so d = 18 x 7 / 4 = 31.5 units. (b) 18 : 4 :: 45 : h, so h = 4 x 45 / 18 = 10 hours. (c) The week has 6 x 6 = 36 hours of sunshine, so 4 : 18 :: 36 : u gives u = 18 x 36 / 4 = 162 units. (d) 162 is more than the science lab's 60 units, so it can run that lab. Both labs need 60 + 110 = 170 units, and 162 is 8 units short, so it cannot run both.
s: Part (a): 31.5 units
Part (b): 10 hours
Part (c): 162 units from 36 hours
Part (d): enough for the science lab (60) but 8 units short for both labs (170)

questions.q:
Problem: 6 notebooks cost Rs 138. Find the cost of 15 notebooks by the Rule of Three. Match each term with its value.
Column A: 1. pramana  2. phala  3. ichchha  4. ichchhaphala
Column B: a. 15 notebooks  b. Rs 138  c. Rs 345  d. 6 notebooks

A school survey found that 35 of every 60 students walk to school. Kiran wants to know how many of the 24 students in her class would walk at the same rate. She writes 24 : x :: 35 : 60 and gets x = 41 1/7. What has gone wrong?
o: Her ratios are in different orders; 60 : 35 :: 24 : x gives 14
Nothing; she should simply round 41 1/7 down to 41 walkers
She should write 35 : 24 :: 60 : x; then 41 1/7 stands
She should first reduce 35 : 60 to 7 : 12; then 41 1/7 is correct
questions.a: Her ratios are in different orders; 60 : 35 :: 24 : x gives 14

questions.q:
The Moon travels about 24 lakh km around the Earth in 27 days. Assume it covers equal distances in equal times.
(a) About how far does it travel in 9 days?
(b) About how many days does it take to travel 40 lakh km?
s: Part (a): 8 lakh km
Part (b): 45 days

questions.q:
A student writes this 'proof': 'If a : b :: c : d, then c = a + f and d = b + f for some number f. So c - a = d - b, and therefore ad = bc.'
(a) What is wrong with the first step?
(b) Write the correct first step.
(c) Starting from your correct first step, derive ad = bc.
(d) Use the true proportion 3 : 5 :: 12 : 20 to show that the student's first step fails.
(e) Use ad = bc to find d in 3 : 5 :: 4.2 : d.
questions.a: (a) It adds the same number to both terms, but proportional ratios come from multiplying both terms by the same factor; adding usually changes the ratio. (b) c = f x a and d = f x b for the same factor f. (c) Then f = c/a and f = d/b, so c/a = d/b; multiplying both sides by ab gives bc = ad. (d) 12 - 3 = 9 but 20 - 5 = 15, so there is no single number f added to both terms, yet the proportion is true (3 x 20 = 60 = 5 x 12). (e) 3 x d = 5 x 4.2 = 21, so d = 7.
s: Part (a): the step adds instead of multiplying by a common factor
Part (b): c = fa and d = fb
Part (c): c/a = d/b, then multiply by ab to get ad = bc
Part (d): differences 9 and 15 differ though the proportion holds
Part (e): d = 7

questions.q:
(a) Write a word problem from daily life whose answer is found by working out (12 x 35) / 8. Say what each of the three numbers stands for.
(b) Write your problem as a proportion a : b :: c : d with d unknown, and show that cross multiplication leads to (12 x 35) / 8.
(c) Solve the problem and explain why the size of the answer makes sense.
questions.a: (a) For example: 8 m of a rope costs Rs 12; find the cost of 35 m of the same rope. 8 is the known length, 12 is its cost in rupees and 35 is the new length. (b) 8 : 12 :: 35 : d. Cross multiplying, 8 x d = 12 x 35, so d = (12 x 35) / 8. (c) d = 420 / 8 = Rs 52.50. This makes sense: 35 m is a little over 4 times 8 m, and Rs 52.50 is a little over 4 times Rs 12.
s: Part (a): a sensible situation naming what 8, 12 and 35 stand for
Part (c): Rs 52.50 (or 52.5 of the unit), with a size check

questions.q: A teacher gives four problems. Which one can correctly be solved with the Rule of Three?
questions.a: 3 m of a cloth cost Rs 270; find the cost of 7 m
o: 3 m of a cloth cost Rs 270; find the cost of 7 m
A trip takes 3 hours at 40 km/h; find the time at 60 km/h
A boy was 120 cm tall at 6; find his height at 15
A mother is 30 and her son 3; find her age when he is 12

questions.q: A school bus covers 72 km in 80 minutes at a steady speed. At the same speed, how far will it go in 2 hours?
questions.a: 108 km

questions.q:
A tour company knows that 4 buses, all full, carried 216 people last year. This year 300 people are going, and the buses are the same size.
(a) Use a proportion to find how many buses 300 people need. What do you notice about the answer?
(b) How many buses must the company hire, and how many seats will be empty?
questions.a: (a) 4 : 216 :: b : 300 gives b = 4 x 300 / 216 = 50/9, about 5.6 buses. A part of a bus cannot be hired, so the proportion gives a fraction that must be rounded up. (b) 6 buses. Each bus seats 216 / 4 = 54, so 6 buses seat 324 and 324 - 300 = 24 seats are empty.
s: Part (a): about 5.6 buses, noting that it is not a whole number
Part (b): 6 buses with 24 empty seats

questions.q:
Assertion (A): If 3 painters take 12 days to paint a school building, then 6 painters working at the same pace will take 24 days, by the Rule of Three.
Reason (R): The Rule of Three can be used only when the two quantities change together by the same multiplying factor.
questions.a: A is false but R is true
o: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

questions.q: A printer prints 45 pages in 1.5 minutes. At the same rate it prints ___ pages in 40 seconds. (Write the number in digits.)

Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: If 5 kg of potatoes cost Rs 140, then 2 kg cost Rs 350, since 5 : 140 :: 2 : d gives d = (140 x 5) / 2.
Statement 2: If 12 identical pens cost Rs 90, then 20 such pens cost Rs 150.
Statement 3: If a 1.5 kg bag of rice costs Rs 96, then a 4 kg bag at the same rate costs Rs 266.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 2 only

questions.q: True or False: A pipe fills a 2-litre jug in 40 seconds, so by the Rule of Three it fills a 750 mL bottle in 15,000 seconds, since 2 : 40 :: 750 : 15,000. Give the reason or the correction.
questions.a: False. The two ratios use different units for volume (litres and millilitres). Writing 2 L as 2,000 mL gives 2,000 : 40 :: 750 : d, so d = 40 x 750 / 2,000 = 15 seconds.
s: States False
Converts 2 L to 2,000 mL and finds 15 seconds

questions.q: During a PE class, a student counts 18 heartbeats in 15 seconds. At this rate, how many times does her heart beat in 2 minutes?

Sana says: 'For the same tap, the time to fill a tank is proportional to the volume of the tank. And for the same tank, the time to fill it is proportional to the number of identical taps used.' Test each part and give your verdict.
questions.a: Partly right. The first part is correct: a tank of twice the volume takes twice the time with the same tap, so volume and time change by the same factor. The second part is wrong: with more taps the tank fills faster, so the time goes down when the number of taps goes up. The two quantities do not increase together, so this is not a direct proportion and the Rule of Three cannot be used for it.
s: Accepts the first part, with a reason
Rejects the second part: more taps means less time
Gives the verdict that the claim is only partly right

questions.q: Which of these tables shows two quantities in direct proportion?
questions.a: Petrol: 2, 5, 8 litres cost Rs 210, 525, 840
o: Tiles: side 2, 5, 8 cm and area 4, 25, 64 sq cm

questions.q:
Town P has an area of 120 sq km and a population of 9,00,000. Town Q has an area of 45 sq km and a population of 4,50,000.
(a) Find the number of people for every 1 sq km in each town.
(b) Which town is more crowded? Explain why comparing the populations alone would mislead.
questions.a: (a) P: 9,00,000 / 120 = 7,500 people per sq km. Q: 4,50,000 / 45 = 10,000 people per sq km. (b) Q is more crowded, since it has more people on each sq km. P has more people in all, but it also has much more land, so the totals alone do not compare crowding; the ratio of people to area does.
s: Part (a): 7,500 and 10,000 people per sq km
Part (b): Q, explaining that area must be taken into account

questions.q: An auto-rickshaw charges a fixed Rs 50 plus Rs 15 for every km. Show that the fare is not proportional to the distance, by comparing the fares for 5 km and 10 km. Then say what the Rule of Three would wrongly predict for 10 km.
questions.a: Fare for 5 km = 50 + 15 x 5 = Rs 125. Fare for 10 km = 50 + 15 x 10 = Rs 200. The distance doubles but the fare does not (125 x 2 = 250, not 200), so 5 : 125 and 10 : 200 are not proportional (1 : 25 against 1 : 20). The Rule of Three, 5 : 125 :: 10 : d, would wrongly predict Rs 250, because the fixed Rs 50 is not charged again.
s: Finds Rs 125 for 5 km and Rs 200 for 10 km
Shows the ratios 1 : 25 and 1 : 20 differ, so there is no proportion
States the wrong prediction Rs 250 and why

questions.q: A family's solar water heater supplies 54,750 litres of hot water in a year of 365 days, the same amount every day. At this rate, how much hot water does it supply in 73 days?
questions.a: 10,950 litres

questions.q:
A stall sells 200 g of groundnuts for Rs 30. A wholesale shop sells a 1.5 kg bag of the same groundnuts for Rs 210.
(a) Write both weight-to-price ratios with the weight in grams, in simplest form, and say whether they are proportional.
(b) Which is cheaper for 1 kg, and by how much?
questions.a: (a) 200 : 30 = 20 : 3 and 1,500 : 210 = 50 : 7. These are different, so the ratios are not proportional. (b) Stall: 1,000 g is 5 times 200 g, so Rs 30 x 5 = Rs 150 per kg. Bag: 1,000 g is 2/3 of 1,500 g, so Rs 210 x 2/3 = Rs 140 per kg. The bag is cheaper by Rs 10 per kg.
s: Part (a): 20 : 3 and 50 : 7, not proportional
Part (b): Rs 150 and Rs 140 per kg, so the bag is cheaper by Rs 10

questions.q:
For each situation, decide whether it is a direct proportion. If it is, solve it with a proportion; if it is not, explain why the Rule of Three cannot be used.
(a) 5 m of an iron pipe weighs 7.5 kg. Find the weight of 12 m of the same pipe.
(b) A girl walks 1.2 km in 15 minutes at a steady pace. How long does she take to walk 4 km?
(c) A girl was 75 cm tall on her first birthday. How tall will she be when she is 16 years old?
(d) A 1 GB data pack costs Rs 19 and a 3 GB pack costs Rs 49. Find the cost of a 6 GB pack.
(e) What single test did you use in every part to decide?
questions.a: (a) Direct: 5 : 7.5 :: 12 : w gives w = 7.5 x 12 / 5 = 18 kg. (b) Direct (steady pace): 1.2 : 15 :: 4 : t gives t = 15 x 4 / 1.2 = 50 minutes. (c) Not direct: a child's height does not grow by the same factor as her age; 1 : 75 :: 16 : h would give h = 1,200 cm = 12 m, which is absurd. (d) Not direct: 1 : 19 and 3 : 49 are not proportional (3 GB would cost Rs 57 at the 1 GB rate), so the prices do not follow one ratio and a 6 GB price cannot be found by the Rule of Three. (e) Whether the two quantities change by the same multiplying factor (increase or decrease together in the same ratio).
s: Part (a): direct, 18 kg
Part (b): direct, 50 minutes
Part (c): not direct, since height does not grow by the same factor as age (12 m is absurd)
Part (d): not direct, since 1 : 19 and 3 : 49 are not proportional
Part (e): the test of change by the same factor

questions.q:
A recipe for lemon rice for 8 people uses 600 g of rice, 30 mL of oil and 2 lemons, and takes 25 minutes to cook. A school camp has 50 people. The storekeeper measures rice in kg and oil in litres.
(a) How much rice is needed, in kg?
(b) How much oil is needed, in litres?
(c) Lemons can only be bought whole. How many lemons are needed?
(d) Rice is sold only in 1 kg packets at Rs 64 each. How many packets must the storekeeper buy, and what do they cost?
(e) A helper says cooking for 50 will take 25 x 50 / 8, about 156 minutes. Can the Rule of Three be used for the cooking time? Explain.
questions.a: (a) 8 : 600 :: 50 : d gives d = 600 x 50 / 8 = 3,750 g = 3.75 kg. (b) 30 x 50 / 8 = 187.5 mL = 0.1875 L. (c) 2 x 50 / 8 = 12.5, so 13 lemons must be bought. (d) 3.75 kg needs 4 packets, since 3 packets give only 3 kg; they cost 4 x 64 = Rs 256. (e) No. The rice, oil and lemons grow with the number of people, but the cooking time does not change by the same factor as the number of people (a bigger pot does not take 50/8 times as long), so time and people are not in direct proportion.
s: Part (a): 3.75 kg
Part (b): 0.1875 L
Part (c): 13 lemons
Part (d): 4 packets for Rs 256
Part (e): no, cooking time does not change by the same factor

questions.q:
A family car covers 54 km in 45 minutes at a steady speed. At the toll plaza, at 10:15 am, they still have 126 km to go to their aunt's town, where lunch is at 12:45 pm. The mother works out the distance they cover in 2 hours by writing 54 : 45 :: d : 2.
(a) What is wrong with the mother's proportion? Write it correctly.
(b) How far does the car go in 2 hours at this speed?
(c) How long will the remaining 126 km take?
(d) They plan a 20-minute stop for fuel and snacks. Will they reach before lunch? Justify.
questions.a: (a) The 45 is in minutes but the 2 is in hours; both times must be in the same unit. Correct form: 54 : 45 :: d : 120 (2 hours = 120 minutes). (b) d = 54 x 120 / 45 = 144 km. (c) 54 : 45 :: 126 : t gives t = 45 x 126 / 54 = 105 minutes = 1 hour 45 minutes. (d) 10:15 am + 1 hour 45 minutes + 20 minutes = 12:20 pm, which is 25 minutes before 12:45 pm, so yes, they will reach before lunch.
s: Part (a): the units differ; uses 120 minutes
Part (b): 144 km
Part (c): 105 minutes
Part (d): yes, arriving at 12:20 pm

questions.q:
A hostel buys washing powder. The shop's price list is:
500 g packet: Rs 60
1 kg packet: Rs 110
4 kg bag: Rs 400
The hostel needs exactly 6 kg this month and wants to spend as little as possible.
(a) Is the price of the 500 g packet proportional to the price of the 1 kg packet? Show using ratios with weight in grams.
(b) Find the price of 1 kg when bought as each size.
(c) Find the cost of each of these ways to buy exactly 6 kg: six 1 kg packets; one 4 kg bag and four 500 g packets; one 4 kg bag and two 1 kg packets.
(d) Which way should the hostel choose? Use your answer to (b) to explain why no other way can be cheaper.
questions.a: (a) 500 : 60 = 25 : 3 and 1,000 : 110 = 100 : 11. These are different (25 : 3 = 100 : 12), so the prices are not proportional. (b) 500 g size: Rs 60 x 2 = Rs 120 per kg; 1 kg size: Rs 110 per kg; 4 kg size: Rs 400 / 4 = Rs 100 per kg. (c) Six 1 kg packets: 6 x 110 = Rs 660. One 4 kg bag and four 500 g packets: 400 + 4 x 60 = Rs 640. One 4 kg bag and two 1 kg packets: 400 + 2 x 110 = Rs 620. (d) One 4 kg bag and two 1 kg packets, for Rs 620. The 4 kg bag is the cheapest per kg, but a second bag would give 8 kg, more than needed; the 2 kg left over is cheapest as 1 kg packets (Rs 110 per kg) rather than 500 g packets (Rs 120 per kg).
s: Part (a): 25 : 3 against 100 : 11, not proportional
Part (b): Rs 120, Rs 110 and Rs 100 per kg
Part (c): Rs 660, Rs 640 and Rs 620
Part (d): one 4 kg bag and two 1 kg packets, using the per-kg prices

questions.q:
A printing shop's price list for visiting cards is: 100 cards for Rs 250, 200 cards for Rs 450, 500 cards for Rs 1,000.
(a) Using the ratio of the number of cards to the price, show whether the price is proportional to the number of cards.
(b) A club needs exactly 300 cards. Raju says, 'By the Rule of Three on the 100-card price, 300 cards cost Rs 750.' Find the cheapest way to buy exactly 300 cards from this list, and say whether Raju's figure is what the club will pay.
questions.a: (a) 100 : 250 = 2 : 5, 200 : 450 = 4 : 9 and 500 : 1,000 = 1 : 2. The simplest forms differ, so the price is not proportional to the number of cards (bigger orders get more cards per rupee). (b) Three lots of 100 cost 3 x 250 = Rs 750, but one lot of 200 and one of 100 cost 450 + 250 = Rs 700. The cheapest way is Rs 700, so Raju's Rs 750 is too high: the price list does not follow one ratio, so the Rule of Three does not give the real price.
s: Part (a): 2 : 5, 4 : 9 and 1 : 2 differ, so not proportional
Part (b): 200 + 100 cards for Rs 700, so Raju's Rs 750 is not the price

questions.q: A recipe uses 400 g of paneer for 5 people. A caterer writes 400 : 5 :: 2 : d to find how many people 2 kg of paneer will serve. What should he do?
questions.a: Change 2 kg to 2,000 g; it serves 25 people
o: Change 2 kg to 2,000 g; it serves 25 people
Change 400 g to 4 kg; it serves 2.5 people
Keep the units; it serves 0.025 people
Change 2 kg to 200 g; it serves 2.5 people

questions.q:
(a) Write a real situation, with units, in which 250 : 6 :: 1,000 : 24 is a correct proportion.
(b) Check by cross multiplication that the proportion is true.
(c) Someone rewrites it as 6 : 250 :: 24 : 1,000. Is this still a correct proportion for your situation? Say what each ratio now compares.
questions.a: (a) For example: 250 g of dough makes 6 rotis, so 1,000 g of dough makes 24 rotis. (b) 250 x 24 = 6,000 and 6 x 1,000 = 6,000, so it is true. (c) Yes. Its cross products are 6 x 1,000 = 6,000 and 250 x 24 = 6,000, which are equal. Both ratios now compare rotis to grams of dough (6 rotis for 250 g, 24 rotis for 1,000 g) instead of dough to rotis; the order is swapped in both ratios, so they stay proportional.
s: Part (a): a sensible situation with matching units
Part (b): both cross products equal 6,000
Part (c): yes, with equal cross products and both ratios now rotis : dough

questions.q: Rs 6,300 is divided between two cousins in the ratio 4 : 5. Kabir says: 'Without finding the shares, I can tell the larger share is Rs 700 more than the smaller.' Is Kabir right? Explain his shortcut and check it by finding both shares.
questions.a: Yes. The ratio 4 : 5 splits Rs 6,300 into 4 + 5 = 9 equal groups of 6,300 / 9 = Rs 700. The larger share has exactly one group more than the smaller, so it is Rs 700 more. Check: 4 x 700 = Rs 2,800 and 5 x 700 = Rs 3,500, and 3,500 - 2,800 = Rs 700.

questions.a: False. The mix has 12 x 1/4 = 3 L of red and 12 x 3/4 = 9 L of yellow. After adding 2 L of yellow there are 3 L of red and 11 L of yellow, so the new ratio is 3 : 11. Adding 2 to the term of the ratio (3 + 2 = 5) is wrong, because the ratio terms are not litres.

A jug holds 880 mL of rose sharbat made with syrup and water in the ratio 3 : 8. Ravi finds it too weak and says, 'I will add only water until the ratio of syrup to water becomes 1 : 2.' questions.a: 880 mL is split into 3 + 8 = 11 parts of 80 mL, so there are 3 x 80 = 240 mL of syrup and 8 x 80 = 640 mL of water. Adding water keeps the syrup at 240 mL. For 1 : 2 the water would have to be 2 x 240 = 480 mL, but there is already 640 mL, and adding water only makes it more. So the ratio can never become 1 : 2 that way (the sharbat only gets weaker). Adding syrup instead: the water stays 640 mL, so for 1 : 2 the syrup must be 640 / 2 = 320 mL, and 320 - 240 = 80 mL of syrup must be added.

questions.q:
Gauri invested Rs 60,000 and Hamid invested Rs 40,000 in a juice stall. Each month's profit is shared in the ratio of what each has invested at that time.
(a) The first month's profit is Rs 15,000. Find each share.
(b) At the start of the second month Hamid invests Rs 20,000 more. The second month's profit is Rs 18,000. Find each share.
(c) Find each partner's total profit for the two months and write the ratio of the totals in simplest form.
(d) Gauri says, 'Our total profits must be in the ratio 3 : 2, because that is how we started.' Is she right?
(e) Hamid hopes that after a third month, with the investments unchanged, the two totals will be equal. Can this happen? Explain.
questions.a: (a) 60,000 : 40,000 = 3 : 2; 15,000 / 5 = 3,000, so Gauri Rs 9,000 and Hamid Rs 6,000. (b) Now 60,000 : 60,000 = 1 : 1, so each gets Rs 9,000. (c) Gauri 9,000 + 9,000 = Rs 18,000; Hamid 6,000 + 9,000 = Rs 15,000; ratio 18,000 : 15,000 = 6 : 5. (d) No. The ratio changed to 1 : 1 in the second month, so the totals are 6 : 5, not 3 : 2. (e) No. With the investments still 1 : 1, every later month adds equal amounts to both, so Gauri stays Rs 3,000 ahead.
s: Part (a): Rs 9,000 and Rs 6,000
Part (b): Rs 9,000 each
Part (c): totals Rs 18,000 and Rs 15,000, ratio 6 : 5
Part (d): no, the totals are 6 : 5
Part (e): no, equal shares keep the Rs 3,000 gap

questions.q:
A school orders 500 medals. Each medal has a mass of 12 g and is made of an alloy of copper and zinc mixed in the ratio 7 : 3 by mass. Copper costs Rs 900 per kg and zinc costs Rs 300 per kg. The school's budget for the metal is Rs 4,000, and the sports teacher wants each medal to contain at least 7 g of copper.
(a) Find the mass of copper and the mass of zinc in one medal.
(b) Find the metal cost of one medal.
(c) Find the metal cost of 500 medals, and say whether it is within the budget.
(d) The maker offers an alloy in the ratio 3 : 2 instead, keeping each medal at 12 g. Find the mass of copper and of zinc in one medal now.
(e) Should the school accept the 3 : 2 alloy? Justify using both the budget and the teacher's condition.
questions.a: (a) 12 g is split into 7 + 3 = 10 parts of 1.2 g, so copper = 7 x 1.2 = 8.4 g and zinc = 3 x 1.2 = 3.6 g. (b) Copper: 900 x 8.4 / 1,000 = Rs 7.56. Zinc: 300 x 3.6 / 1,000 = Rs 1.08. One medal: 7.56 + 1.08 = Rs 8.64. (c) 500 x 8.64 = Rs 4,320, which is Rs 320 over the budget. (d) 12 g is split into 3 + 2 = 5 parts of 2.4 g, so copper = 3 x 2.4 = 7.2 g and zinc = 2 x 2.4 = 4.8 g. (e) Yes. One medal now costs 900 x 7.2 / 1,000 + 300 x 4.8 / 1,000 = 6.48 + 1.44 = Rs 7.92, so 500 medals cost Rs 3,960, which is Rs 40 within the budget. Each medal still has 7.2 g of copper, at least the 7 g the teacher wants. The 3 : 2 alloy meets both conditions; the 7 : 3 alloy fails the budget.
s: Part (a): 8.4 g of copper and 3.6 g of zinc
Part (b): Rs 7.56 + Rs 1.08 = Rs 8.64, converting grams to kg
Part (c): Rs 4,320, over the budget by Rs 320
Part (d): 7.2 g of copper and 4.8 g of zinc
Part (e): yes: Rs 3,960 is within Rs 4,000 and 7.2 g is at least 7 g

questions.q:
An artist has a 300 mL tin of green paint made by mixing blue and yellow in the ratio 2 : 3. By mistake she pours in 60 mL more yellow. She needs at least 300 mL of the original shade (blue : yellow = 2 : 3) for a mural. Blue paint is sold in 50 mL tubes at Rs 40 and in 25 mL tubes at Rs 25. She may use part of a tube and keep the rest. A new 300 mL tin of the original shade costs Rs 180.
(a) How much blue and how much yellow were in the tin at first?
(b) What is the ratio of blue to yellow after the mistake, in simplest form?
(c) How much blue must she add to get back to the ratio 2 : 3?
(d) What is the cheapest way for her to have at least 300 mL of the original shade: fix the spoilt paint with 50 mL tubes, fix it with 25 mL tubes, or buy a new tin? Justify with the amounts and costs.
questions.a: (a) 300 is split into 2 + 3 = 5 parts of 60 mL: blue 120 mL, yellow 180 mL. (b) Yellow is now 240 mL, so 120 : 240 = 1 : 2. (c) For 2 : 3 with 240 mL of yellow, blue must be 240 x 2/3 = 160 mL, so she adds 160 - 120 = 40 mL of blue. (d) Fix it with one 50 mL tube. One 50 mL tube (Rs 40) covers the 40 mL. One 25 mL tube is not enough, so 25 mL tubes need two (Rs 50). A new tin costs Rs 180. Fixing gives 160 + 240 = 400 mL of the original shade, which is at least 300 mL, so one 50 mL tube for Rs 40 is the cheapest way.
s: Part (a): 120 mL blue and 180 mL yellow
Part (b): 1 : 2
Part (c): add 40 mL of blue
Part (d): one 50 mL tube for Rs 40 (against Rs 50 and Rs 180), giving 400 mL

Two classes collected old newspapers for recycling: Class 8A collected 96 kg and Class 8B collected 64 kg. The scrap dealer paid Rs 1,750 for all of it, and the money is shared between the classes in the ratio of the kilograms collected. The principal then adds a prize of Rs 250. 8B's monitor wants the prize split equally; 8A's monitor wants it split in the same ratio as the newspaper money.
(a) Write the ratio of the newspapers collected by 8A and 8B in simplest form.
(b) Find each class's share of the Rs 1,750.
(c) Find each class's share of the prize if it is split in the same ratio.

(d) Split equally, each class gets Rs 125. 8B gets Rs 125 instead of Rs 100, which is Rs 25 more, so splitting equally gives 8B more.
s: Part (a): 3 : 2
Part (b): Rs 1,050 and Rs 700
Part (c): Rs 150 and Rs 100
Part (d): equal split, Rs 25 more for 8B

questions.q:
When a quantity x is divided in the ratio m : n, the first part is (m x x) / (m + n).
(a) Explain why this part is always less than x (for m and n greater than 0).
(b) When is the first part more than half of x? Give a reason and an example.
questions.a: (a) The first part is x multiplied by m/(m + n). Since m is less than m + n, this fraction is less than 1, so the part is less than x. (b) When m is greater than n: then m is more than half of m + n, so the first part is more than half of x. For example, 60 in the ratio 2 : 1 gives 40 and 20, and 40 is more than 30.
s: Part (a): m/(m + n) is less than 1
Part (b): when m is greater than n, with an example

Land in a village costs Rs 21,78,000 per acre (1 acre = 43,560 sq ft). A family looks at two plots: Plot X is 60 ft by 90 ft, and Plot Y is exactly 1/8 of an acre. Their budget is Rs 2,75,000, and they must also pay a registration fee of Rs 5,000 on whichever plot they buy.

questions.a: (a) 2 x 2.471 = 4.942 acres; 2 x 10,000 = 20,000 sq m. (b) From square metres: 20,000 x 10.764 = 2,15,280 sq ft. From acres: 4.942 x 43,560 = 2,15,273.52 sq ft. (c) The conversion factors 2.471 and 10.764 are rounded to three decimal places, so the two routes give slightly different answers (a difference of under 7 sq ft out of more than 2 lakh). It is not a mistake; both are correct to the accuracy of the factors.

Part (c): rounding in the factors explains the small difference; not a mistake

(a) Write the tank's capacity in millilitres.
(b) How many seconds does the pump take to fill the empty tank?
(c) Write this time in hours and minutes.

(e) One morning the tank already holds 300 litres when the caretaker switches the pump on at 7:20 am. He tells the principal, 'It will be full before 9:00 am.' Is he right? If not, by how many minutes is he off?
questions.a: (a) 1,200 x 1,000 = 12,00,000 mL. (b) 500 : 4 :: 12,00,000 : t, so t = 4 x 12,00,000 / 500 = 9,600 seconds. (c) 9,600 / 60 = 160 minutes = 2 hours 40 minutes. (d) 6:30 am + 2 hours 40 minutes = 9:10 am. (e) No. Only 1,200 - 300 = 900 litres = 9,00,000 mL are needed, which take 4 x 9,00,000 / 500 = 7,200 seconds = 2 hours. Starting at 7:20 am, the tank is full at 9:20 am, so he is off by 20 minutes.
s: Part (b): 9,600 seconds
Part (c): 2 hours 40 minutes
Part (d): 9:10 am
Part (e): no; 900 litres take 2 hours, full at 9:20 am, 20 minutes later than he said

A travel website lists the maximum temperatures for one day in degrees Fahrenheit: Shimla 59, Chennai 95, Leh 23 and Ooty 72.5. A school will take its trip only to a place whose maximum temperature is from 10 to 30 degrees Celsius. (d) Shimla: (5/9) x (59 - 32) = (5/9) x 27 = 15 degrees Celsius. Chennai (35) is too hot and Leh (-5) too cold. Shimla (15) and Ooty (22.5) both lie from 10 to 30. Ooty is 2.5 degrees from 20 and Shimla is 5 degrees from 20, so the school chooses Ooty.
s: Part (a): 35 degrees Celsius
Part (b): -5 degrees Celsius
Part (c): 22.5 degrees Celsius
Part (d): Ooty, as Shimla (15) and Ooty (22.5) qualify and Ooty is nearer 20

Shop B: 7 bags give only 350 kg, so he needs 8 bags (400 kg) costing 8 x 2,600 = Rs 20,800. He should buy 15 bags from Shop A for Rs 20,250, which is Rs 550 cheaper.

Part (b): 370.65 kg

(c) A student works out (9/5) x (180 + 32) instead. Find the student's answer and explain what the student did in the wrong order.
questions.a: (a) For example: a cake recipe says to bake at 180 degrees Celsius, but the oven dial is marked only in degrees Fahrenheit. What should the dial be set to? 180 is the temperature in degrees Celsius, and the answer is the same temperature in degrees Fahrenheit. (b) (9/5) x 180 = 324, and 324 + 32 = 356 degrees Fahrenheit.
